note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Runny nose, nasal congestion, cough, ear pulling, and fever

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient with upper respiratory symptoms beginning around supper time last night. Presents with clear nasal drainage, nasal congestion, and non-barky cough. Reports ear pulling and frequent nasal rubbing. Rectal temperature measured by parent was 100.3°F. Appetite reduced - patient consumed approximately 7 ounces from bottle this morning and barely finished additional bottle; declined cereal. Patient irritable and difficult to settle for sleep despite maintaining good energy level. Exposure history significant for older sister currently ill with similar symptoms and recent playdate with cousin who had sinus infection. Parent has attempted conservative management with saline nasal mist, acetaminophen given early this morning, baby Vick's applied to feet overnight, and humidifier use. Additionally, cradle cap has worsened.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: Irritability, decreased appetite, difficulty settling to sleep
Head, Eyes, Ears, Nose, Throat: Clear nasal drainage, nasal congestion, non-barky cough, ear pulling, nasal rubbing
Integumentary: Worsening cradle cap
All other systems reviewed and negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
None documented

MEDICATIONS
Saline nasal spray
Acetaminophen
Baby Vick's vaporub
Aveno shampoo

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Older sister currently ill with upper respiratory infection

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with parent and older sister; recent exposure to cousin with sinus infection

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Rectal temperature 100.3°F
General: Well-appearing, cooperative child
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally with excellent breath sounds
Ears: No acute findings on otoscopic examination
Remainder of examination: Unremarkable

RESULTS
COVID-19: Negative

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Viral upper respiratory infection
- Currently appears to be viral infection; antibiotics not indicated at this time
- Monitor closely for development of barking cough, which would indicate more significant disease
- Encourage continued fluids and rest
- If barking cough develops, administer half teaspoon of prescribed cough medicine for 5 days
- For regular cough, may use Zarbee's cough syrup using dosing for children under one year of age
- Parent counseled to avoid honey in children under one year of age; agave is acceptable alternative
- Prescription for cough medicine provided to have on hand given weekend proximity; only use if barking cough develops
- Follow-up appointment in 1 week
- Advise to return if symptoms worsen or barking cough develops

2. Cradle cap (Seborrheic dermatitis)
- Recommend dandruff shampoo such as Head & Shoulders, Selsun Blue, or Nizoral AD (regular strength, not extra strength)
- Apply twice weekly with two days between applications; use regular shampoo on other days
- Continue gentle brushing and baby oil to assist with scale removal
- Expected improvement within approximately 6 weeks with regular use
- Important to avoid shampoo contact with eyes during rinsing
- Return if condition worsens despite treatment
- Follow-up in 1 week
